work_order.understanding: The plan PR #91 was built from was not wrong about the cause. Its diagnosis holds: PR #9 (squash 026f8b6) shipped a user-visible custom-report fix with nothing under upcoming-release-notes/, the composite action .github/actions/release-notes/check/action.yml is referenced by no workflow, and ci-verify.yml runs typecheck, lint, unit, build and e2e only — so the release-note requirement is advisory and a squashed bot-authored PR slipped past it. The remedy it chose, a unit-test gate over the real notes directory, is the right shape given that .github/** is forbidden to every plan. What was wrong was the shipped gate, in two independent ways QA measured, and neither is a wrong acceptance criterion so none is rewritten: AC-1..AC-4 are kept verbatim and AC-5 (nested-note escape) and AC-6 (cache-skipped gate) are added after them. (1) The gate enumerated upcoming-release-notes/ with a single non-recursive fs.readdirSync, copying its inclusion rule from parseReleaseNotes rather than from selectReleaseNotePaths (util.mjs:129-156, fed by the recursive git diff pathspec), so a nested note is selected by the release-notes checker and counted by count-points.mjs while escaping the unit gate (gap-nested-note.txt, GATE_EXIT=0; T-13 failed on those bytes). (2) The gate lives inside lage's cached `test` task and no release note can ever enter that task's hash: QA measured the same key d1677e96… with `» skip @actual-app/ci-actions test` and exit 0 on bytes direct vitest rejects with exit 1, across four standalone evidence files. This makes the plan's central claim — that the suite runs in CI on every PR — true only on a cold cache. T-12's literal assertion failure is its own control, not the behaviour under test: `withNote` is declared async with a synchronous body, so the note is already restored when the control's vitestGate() runs, and the control throws before the assertion under test is reached. That is a defect in QA's spec and does not clear the product defect. Answering the outstanding plan-review objection, the only reason the previous work order was refused: AC-6's how_to_verify told the reader to restore the note at step (4) and then required `yarn test` at step (5) to exit non-zero with the same message, so the criterion could only be satisfied by a gate that fires on a valid note. Its steps (4)-(5) are rewritten to the reviewer's first option, keeping both halves the check text claims and adding a no-false-positive half: (4) with the note still broken, `yarn test` → non-zero with the same message; (5) restore the note and run `yarn test` again → exit 0 with no release-notes failure. Every step now asserts about the state the note is actually in at that step. Nothing else changes. Limits, stated plainly: this checkout has no node_modules, so neither defect was re-executed here. The nested-note blindness was reproduced with a standalone node script over the shipped readdirSync logic, and the cache behaviour and every lage mechanism the approach depends on were read out of the exact tarball the lockfile pins (lage 2.15.17) rather than assumed — WrappedTarget.successful is `status === 'skipped' || status === 'success'`; TargetFactory writes `cache: s.cache !== false`; the worker's runTargetWithCaching returns cacheHit:false and runs whenever `!target.cache`; getReadyTargets admits a target only when every dependency is successful, so the cache lookup for `test` happens after the gate has already run; expandDepSpecs maps a bare dependsOn entry to the same package's task; runAction sets process.exitCode = 1 whenever results !== 'success'; and NpmScriptRunner.shouldRun returns false for a package whose package.json lacks the script, which lands in onSkipped and so still counts as successful. AC-6 is written as the command sequence that will actually execute it. `version` is deliberately left unset: the prompt forbids setting it, the schema requires it, and .github/workflows/sdlc-root-cause.yml:540-547 runs bump-version.mjs BEFORE validation precisely to resolve that, so preflight's "missing required property version" is the known artifact of preflighting before the bump — check-forbidden.mjs (6 paths, none forbidden) and check-split-criteria.mjs (every IAC-n answered) both pass.
work_order.root_cause: Two independent defects, both introduced by the gate this PR added to packages/ci-actions/bin/release-notes-check.test.mjs. (1) NON-RECURSIVE ENUMERATION — readNotes() enumerates upcoming-release-notes/ one level deep, and its inclusion rule was copied from parseReleaseNotes (also non-recursive) rather than from selectReleaseNotePaths (util.mjs:148-149, fed by a recursive `git diff` pathspec, excluding only the top-level README.md); the two functions that read the same directory already disagree and the gate copied the wrong one, so a nested note is checked by the release-notes checker, counted by count-points.mjs and published in the changelog while escaping the gate. (2) THE GATE LIVES INSIDE A CACHED TASK WHOSE INPUTS CANNOT CONTAIN A RELEASE NOTE — `yarn test` is `lage test --continue`; lage hashes each target's inputs, and by construction those inputs can never include upcoming-release-notes/**, because PackageTree.addToPackageTree buckets every tracked file under the nearest ancestor workspace package and the notes directory has none. A note-only change leaves the hash untouched, lage prints `» skip @actual-app/ci-actions test - <same hash>` and exits 0 on a note the checker rejects — the gate is a no-op on precisely the change it exists to police.
work_order.approach: Extract the gate into packages/ci-actions/bin/release-notes-gate.mjs — recursive walk, inclusion rule matching selectReleaseNotePaths (every *.md at any depth, README.md excluded only at the top level), rules from ../src/release-notes/util.mjs plus the two checks validateFile contributes, failure strings keyed by the relative path with forward slashes and otherwise byte-identical to the ones QA's T-8/T-9/T-10 assert, YAML parse errors reported rather than thrown. It runs as a CLI when invoked directly. The vitest block in release-notes-check.test.mjs imports it instead of carrying its own copy, keeps its existing cases, and gains two: one reproducing T-13 by writing upcoming-release-notes/qa-nested/bad-note.md and asserting the failure names `qa-nested/bad-note.md`, and one reproducing T-12's cause structurally by asserting the wiring. Make the gate reachable on a warm cache: add `"release-notes": "node bin/release-notes-gate.mjs"` to packages/ci-actions/package.json, and a `cache: false` `release-notes` pipeline task that `test` dependsOn, in lage.config.js — verified against the lage 2.15.17 bundle the lockfile pins rather than assumed: expandDepSpecs maps a bare dependsOn entry to the same package's task; TargetFactory turns `cache: false` into target.cache = false and the worker's runTargetWithCaching then returns cacheHit:false, so an uncached target always runs; SimpleScheduler.getReadyTargets requires every dependency to be successful while the cache lookup for `test` lives in WrappedTarget.run() after that point, so the gate runs on every invocation even when `test` itself is a cache hit; a gate failure leaves dependents pending, which keeps results !== 'success' and makes runAction set process.exitCode = 1. Packages without the script are skipped cleanly by NpmScriptRunner.shouldRun returning false, which lands in onSkipped — and WrappedTarget.successful counts skipped as successful, so their `test` targets are unaffected. The note file itself does not change.

assumptions: lage 2.15.17 is what the job installs — read from yarn.lock (`lage@npm:2.15.17`) and verified against that exact tarball, not against whatever a newer release happens to do
`yarn test` is `lage test --continue` and ci-verify.yml's 'Unit tests' step runs it, so a failed dependency target in that graph fails the CI step
The lage cache directory QA used (node_modules/.cache/lage) is where it lands for this repo; the AC-6 steps rm it explicitly rather than assume
No other workspace package defines a `release-notes` script today, and adding the key to @actual-app/ci-actions is the only change needed to scope the task
QA writes its hostile spec against this work order, so the test counts it will assert (10 in the file, 73 in the package) are stated in tests[] rather than left to be guessed
unknowns: Whether `yarn test` in AC-6 step (5) exits 0 depends on every other workspace package's tests being green in QA's environment; if one is flaky the step could fail for an unrelated reason. The criterion's wording requires no release-notes failure in the output as well, but the exit code itself is environment-dependent.

AC-5's how_to_verify expects `Validated 92 release note(s).` — that is the count on this branch (92 existing + 1 new). If the note count on the branch at QA time differs, the number in that expected string is stale even though the criterion's substance holds.

I did not execute the fixed gate. The recursion and the exact failure strings are derived from util.mjs and from the strings QA's T-8/T-9/T-10 assert today, but the byte-identity of those strings under the new module is an implementation claim the implementer should check against the shipped gate's own output.
residual_risks: lage's optimisation pass (optimizeTargetGraph) was not traced in full. If it ever dropped a `release-notes` target from the graph the gate would silently stop running — the AC-6 sequence is what would catch that, which is why it is an acceptance criterion rather than a test.
The gate adds one process per `yarn test` run over 93 markdown files. Measured cost is not known from here; if it is material the fix is to narrow the walk, not to re-cache the task.

AC-5 asserts a nested note is held to the same rules, which is a stronger contract than the product strictly needs today, because QA found parseReleaseNotes (util.mjs:158-165) is also non-recursive and a nested note therefore never reaches the published changelog. The checker does select it, so the gate and the checker disagree about the same directory, and closing that is the point — but the user-visible impact of this half is smaller than AC-5's wording implies.

review.title: AC-1 claims CI proves that exactly one note was added and that no other note was modified, renamed or deleted. It cannot. The new case enumerates whatever .md files happen to exist and asserts their content is well-formed; it has no notion of what a diff added, removed or renamed, so every one of those four outcomes is invisible to it. I deleted a pre-existing note outright and the suite stayed green.
review.detail:
AC-1 claims CI proves that exactly one note was added and that no other note was modified, renamed or deleted. It cannot. The new case enumerates whatever .md files happen to exist and asserts their content is well-formed; it has no notion of what a diff added, removed or renamed, so every one of those four outcomes is invisible to it. I deleted a pre-existing note outright and the suite stayed green.

`packages/ci-actions/bin/release-notes-check.test.mjs:293`

Evidence: Ran the negative control the work order never ran: `rm upcoming-release-notes/fix-custom-report-legend-scroll.md` then `npx vitest --run bin/release-notes-check.test.mjs` -> 'Test Files 1 passed (1) / Tests 8 passed (8)'. A deletion is the cleanest possible miss and the gate does not notice. The mechanism is structural: `readNotes()` is `fs.readdirSync(NOTES_DIR).filter(...)` over live working-tree files, so a file that is absent is simply absent from the input set -- there is no expected-file list to diff against. `validateFile()`'s counterpart logic, `selectReleaseNotePaths()`, is the part that reads a diff, and this case calls none of it. The PR body's AC-1 reads '...and no other note is added, modified, renamed or deleted. PROVEN BY CI ... Cite "ci" in this criterion's test_ids.' Note that AC-1's own how_to_verify already gives the correct route (`git diff --name-status origin/main...HEAD -- upcoming-release-notes/`, expecting exactly one A row) -- it is only the 'PROVEN BY CI / Cite ci' sentence that is false. This is the same defect class that got the previous version of this plan rejected: a criterion pointed at a proof route that cannot carry it.

Fix: Drop the 'PROVEN BY CI ... Cite "ci"' sentence from AC-1 and let QA cite the git-diff route its how_to_verify already specifies. The criterion stays provable -- `git diff --name-status origin/main...HEAD -- upcoming-release-notes/` returning exactly one row is the real proof that nothing else moved. Do not try to make the unit case detect additions or deletions; detecting a *missing* note needs a diff, and the diff-selection half of the checker is exactly what lives under .github/** and is out of scope here.

`packages/ci-actions/bin/release-notes-check.test.mjs:293`

Evidence: The assertion is `expect(readNotes().flatMap(validate)).toEqual([])` and `validate()` pushes all six failure kinds -- missing category, unknown category, missing authors, non-list authors, empty authors list, non-person authors, and multi-line body. My negative control B changed only the author to `github-actions` and the failing output was 'fix-custom-report-show-empty-rows-categories.md authors are not people: github-actions' under that category-worded test name; negative control A produced 'body should contain exactly one line' under the same name. The message itself is precise and names the file and the rule, so this costs orientation, not diagnosis.

Fix: Rename the case to describe what it asserts, e.g. 'every note satisfies the published-changelog rules'. The failure strings already carry the specifics; only the title needs widening.

review.title: The new describe block shadows an existing module-scope constant of the same name with a different type and meaning. Line 27 is the relative string 'upcoming-release-notes' used to build throwaway repos; line 231 is an absolute path to the real one. review.title: The 'contains release notes to check' case is justified by a comment describing a failure mode the code cannot have. It exists so a moved or mis-resolved NOTES_DIR cannot make the rule case pass vacuously — but a mis-resolved path throws rather than passing vacuously, and the throw fails the run loudly, which is the better outcome the case is credited with providing.

review.detail:
PR #91's title lacks the mandatory `[AI]` prefix, which .github/agents/pr-and-commit-rules.md requires of every PR and which the agent must apply itself. The work order lists PR #9's squashed title under out_of_scope, but that does not exempt the PR this branch opens.

Evidence: `gh pr view 91 --json title` -> 'fix: The shipped custom-report fix gets the release note the repository requires'. The rules file states 'ALL pull request titles MUST be prefixed with `[AI]` — you have to apply it yourself', with the counter-example 'Fix type error in account validation (MISSING PREFIX — NOT ALLOWED)'. Every recent commit on this branch carries the prefix, so the convention is live. I checked the body too: it uses '## Changed' and '## Acceptance criteria', not the template's Description/Related issue(s)/Testing/Checklist sections, so the do-not-fill-the-template rule is not at issue.

Fix: Retitle to `[AI] fix: The shipped custom-report fix gets the release note the repository requires`. One edit, no code change.

qa_open_bugs.title: `yarn test` silently skips the new release-note gate when only a note changed, so a malformed note passes locally
The new gate reads upcoming-release-notes/ non-recursively, so a note in a subdirectory is never validated

errors: the plan reviewer rejected this revision: AC-6 as written can only be satisfied by a gate that fires on a valid note. Its how_to_verify restores the note at step (4) and then requires `yarn test` at step (5) to exit non-zero with `body should contain exactly one line`. — Rewrite AC-6's how_to_verify steps (4)-(5) so the note's state at each step agrees with what that step asserts. Either: `; (4) with the note still broken, \`yarn test\` -> non-zero with the same message; (5) restore the note and \`yarn test\` -> exit 0` — which keeps both halves the criterion claims (the scoped run and the full monorepo run) on a broken note while also proving no false positive on a clean tree; or drop step (5) and let the sequence end at the scoped rerun, leaving the check text's `The same holds through \`yarn test\` itself` standing on the positive half alone. What must not survive is a step that restores the note followed by a step that expects the restored tree to fail.
